body: So far, we have only really used this for version control systems, I would prefer to keep this with the regular scanner and the related options.

diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+
+#[derive(Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]
+#[cfg_attr(
+    feature = "config-schema",
+    derive(schemars::JsonSchema),
+    schemars(deny_unknown_fields)
+)]
+#[serde(default)]
+pub struct GodotConfig<'a> {
+    pub format: &'a str,
+    pub version_format: &'a str,
+    pub style: &'a str,
+    pub symbol: &'a str,
+    pub disabled: bool,
+    pub show_version: bool,
+    pub version_command: Vec<&'a str>,
+}
+
+impl<'a> Default for GodotConfig<'a> {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        GodotConfig {
+            format: "via [$symbol($version )]($style)",
+            version_format: "v${raw}",
+            style: "bold blue",
+            symbol: "godot ",
+            disabled: false,
+            show_version: false,
body: There is no need for an explicit `show_version` because users can just remove `$version` from the format string instead. If the command is too slow, I would prefer disabling the module by default instead.
I would prefer a regex or `split` & `take_while` here. Instead of only counting dots, please also make sure the text in-between is only compromised of digits.

body:
The reason for not showing the version by default is not because of slowness but because the godot executable is not guaranteed to be in the user's path or have a consistent name.

Would it be acceptable to just remove `$version` from the default format string?

Is the ancestor scan reserved for VCS due to performance reasons? If so, would it be better to just have this module disabled by default?

I'd prefer to keep the ancestor scan for a couple reasons:

1. One of the common godot file extensions, `.gd`, is apparently shared by another project called [GD Graphics Library](https://libgd.github.io/), so searching for this extension could lead to false positives.
2. Personally, I like to know that I'm within a godot project folder even if I'm currently in an organizational subdirectory that doesn't contain any godot-specific file formats.
I pushed an update that uses `split`, `take`, and `take_while` here, and I also updated the unit tests to more thoroughly cover this function.

body: For other modules with slow CLIs, we have disabled them by default, so I would prefer doing that for consistency.
If the module is disabled by default, adding `gd` should be less of an issue.
If the module was disabled by default, wouldn't the ancestor scan also be less of an issue?
